title: Fleet Availability and Utilization
body: At ADW the constraint is rarely broken iron — dump trucks and primary excavators run availability in the 90s while utilization lags 15–25 points behind. That gap is recoverable production sitting idle, and an available excavator standing still costs the same lost BCM as a broken one, minus the repair bill.
keyPoints: Read availability against utilization, never utilization alone. High avail + low util is a sequencing or dispatch problem you can fix today; low avail + low util belongs to the workshop. The two demand different responses.
Start at the summary block — the seven-fleet roll-up tells you which fleet is the day's constraint in one view before you dig into unit rows.

For available-but-idle fleets, the standby reason columns are the diagnosis: "no job," "no material," "no location," and "waiting for GC" separate dispatch problems from face-access and loading-chain problems.

Don't run a machine on restarts between fault windows. EX-263 accumulated 144+ breakdown hours on the same hydraulic fault before anyone ordered a workshop strip — a recurring fault that survives three days of quick fixes needs to come out of the dig plan for root cause.
Watch the quiet fleets: water bowser and grader utilization feed straight into dust, visibility, and haul-road condition — their weakness shows up as everyone else's cycle-time loss.
apply: Drill fleet availability hit 70.83% yesterday — the July low — with DR-343 on a full 24-hour breakdown and DR-297 leaking hydraulics into the drifter; check whether those two are getting root-cause attention or just restart attempts.
